subject: Performance SLO / Concurrency follow-up — Acme Corp (rate limits & quota)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Reed <jon.reed@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO sync — follow-up and next steps

Hi Jonathan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call with the engineering team and a proposed next step list: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- 99th percentile tail latency target: 300ms for short-chat generation (<= 128 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 qps for embedding lookups across several endpoints; peak bursts to 4,000 qps for short windows
- Concurrency: ~250 parallel in-flight requests per region, with connection pooling from 50 application instances
- Streaming: streaming token-level responses required for the chat UI (latency budget for first token < 120ms)

Next steps I proposed:
1) You send the concurrency/traffic matrix (per endpoint, baseline vs peak) — you mentioned Ops would share a spreadsheet
2) We’ll map the traffic to Redwood Dedicated capacity and provide a rate-limit/quota proposal + cost estimate
3) If needed, we’ll propose a canary with a reduced concurrency profile to validate tail latency

I’ve attached the template for the concurrency matrix to make it easy. Can you share the filled sheet by EOD Friday so my infra team can size this?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: acme_concurrency_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jonathan Reed <jon.reed@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO sync — follow-up and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the concurrency matrix — apologies for the slightly messy export. Key clarifications below so your sizing is accurate:

- Traffic profile (p95/p99): baseline 1,200 qps (embedding and short-generation mix), evenings + product launches cause spikes to ~3.8k qps for 10-15 minute bursts.
- Concurrency: our app opens ~50 persistent connections per region from our connection pool; each connection may multiplex ~5 parallel requests depending on client-side batching, so target in-flight concurrency ~= 250 as discussed.
- Streaming: we must support chunked token streaming to the browser; first token should be under 120ms from request arrival at Redwood. We will accept multi-model fallbacks for heavy load provided the fallback model meets p95 latency < 600ms.
- Security: we'll need the rate limits enforced at the tenant level, and logs/audit for each token request for compliance.

I’ve attached the filled matrix: acme_concurrency_requirements.xlsx. Feel free to loop in infra folks if you need more telemetry.

Jonathan Reed
Head of Product Engineering, Acme Corp
jon.reed@acme.com
Attachment: acme_concurrency_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Reed <jon.reed@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO sync — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Jonathan — got the matrix, this is super helpful. High-level proposed approach below; attaching a short proposal PDF that maps your traffic to our rate-limit tiers.

Redwood proposal (initial sizing):
- Dedicated pool sizing: target capacity to sustain baseline 1.2k qps with headroom for 2x sustained, and burst absorb for 4k qps using autoscale/burst nodes — maps to 8 GPU units in region for pilot.
- Tenant-level rate limits: soft quota of 1.5k qps with hard quota enforcement at 4k qps for short bursts. We recommend a 10s token-bucket smoothing window (configurable).
- Connection pooling: honor up to 50 persistent connections per client, with recommended client multiplex factor of 5; we will expose per-connection metrics so you can tune multiplexing.
- Streaming SLOs: first token SLO at 120ms p95 with fallback policy to a slightly smaller model if p95 > 600ms; we'll instrument real-time traces to validate.
- Audit/logging: request-level logs and token counts retained per your retention policy (we discussed SOC 2 needs) — export via secure S3/Cloud Storage or pull via API.

Pricing & next steps:
1) If this sizing looks good, we’ll generate a formal quote (Dedicated monthly commit + per-token usage overage).
2) Optional pilot: 30-day pilot at reduced committed capacity (6 GPU units) to validate tail latency in your real traffic.
3) Rishi will scope the traffic shaping and autoscale configs for the pilot and produce a rollout plan.

Attached: redwood_rate_limits_proposal.pdf (PDF) and the pilot checklist. Do you want us to include a canary plan for rollouts (we usually do a 10% traffic cutover first)?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_rate_limits_proposal.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO / Concurrency follow-up — Acme Corp (rate limits & quota)

Marissa / Rishi — quick internal note before I reply to Jonathan with the formal quote:

- Rishi: please validate the 8 GPU unit estimate against the traffic matrix and confirm if we can fit the pilot into 6 units with degraded headroom but same streaming SLOs (we may need to tighten multiplexing guidance).
- Marissa: include a canary plan in the quote (10% traffic for 48 hours) and an explicit SL rollback trigger (p95 latency > 600ms for 30 minutes).
- Also confirm audit/log export cadence (daily vs hourly) and retention defaults to propose to Acme.

If we can turn this around today I’ll approve the pilot discount line and sign off on the SLA exceptions.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
